## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/single-cell-rna-seq-beginners-guide-part-5-cell-type-specific-differential-expression-proportion-testing-and-functional-pathway-analysis/>

Part 1 of 4. Starting from the annotated Seurat object produced in tutorial 4,
this notebook asks whether the *composition* of the sample changes between
conditions: per-sample cell type proportions are tabulated, plotted, and tested
with `speckle::propeller()` (arcsine-square-root transformation, linear model,
empirical Bayes moderation, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR).

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks. Changes made for this
notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter, paths built
from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and the fixes marked `FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Proportion analysis
library(speckle)

# Visualization and data manipulation
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_5_differential_analysis/tut5_differential_analysis_part1.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
diff.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$diff.subdir)

# Create output directories
for (d in c("plots/proportions", "results")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(diff.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(diff.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Column names, condition levels and colors from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
condition.levels <- c(params$condition.ref, params$condition.test)
condition.colors <- setNames(unlist(params$condition.palette), condition.levels)
```

## Load annotated Seurat object from tutorial 4

```{r step2_load_obj}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Load annotated Seurat object from tutorial 4
#-----------------------------------------------

annotated.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$annot.subdir, params$annotated.rds)
cat("Reading in annotated Seurat object:", annotated.file, "\n")
seurat_obj <- readRDS(annotated.file)

stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, sample.col, condition.col) %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)))
stopifnot(all(condition.levels %in% seurat_obj@meta.data[[condition.col]]))

cat("Cells:", ncol(seurat_obj), "\n")
print(table(seurat_obj@meta.data[[sample.col]], seurat_obj@meta.data[[condition.col]]))
```

## Calculate cell type proportions per sample

```{r step3_proportions}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Calculate cell type proportions per sample
#-----------------------------------------------

# Calculate proportions for each sample
proportion_data <- seurat_obj@meta.data %>%
  group_by(.data[[sample.col]], .data[[condition.col]], .data[[celltype.col]]) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(.data[[sample.col]]) %>%
  mutate(
    total_cells = sum(count),
    proportion = count / total_cells,
    percentage = proportion * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Save proportion data
write.csv(proportion_data, file.path(diff.dir, "results/cell_type_proportions_per_sample.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Display summary
proportion_summary <- proportion_data %>%
  group_by(.data[[condition.col]], .data[[celltype.col]]) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_percentage = mean(percentage),
    sd_percentage = sd(percentage),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(as.data.frame(proportion_summary), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Visualize proportions

```{r step4_proportion_plots, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Visualize cell type proportions
#-----------------------------------------------

# Stacked barplot showing composition of each sample
p_stacked <- ggplot(proportion_data,
                    aes(x = .data[[sample.col]], y = percentage, fill = .data[[celltype.col]])) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(vars(.data[[condition.col]]), scales = "free_x") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "right") +
  labs(title = "Cell Type Composition by Sample",
       x = "Sample", y = "Percentage (%)",
       fill = "Cell Type") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3")
print(p_stacked)

ggsave(file.path(diff.dir, "plots/proportions/01_stacked_composition.png"), p_stacked,
       width = 12, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Grouped barplot with error bars
# FIX: the article's code plots columns `mean` and `sd`, but the summary table
# above names them `mean_percentage` and `sd_percentage`
p_grouped <- ggplot(proportion_summary,
                    aes(x = .data[[celltype.col]], y = mean_percentage, fill = .data[[condition.col]])) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_percentage - sd_percentage, ymax = mean_percentage + sd_percentage),
                position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Mean Cell Type Proportions by Condition",
       x = "Cell Type", y = "Mean Percentage (%)", fill = "Condition") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = condition.colors)
print(p_grouped)

ggsave(file.path(diff.dir, "plots/proportions/02_grouped_proportions.png"), p_grouped,
       width = 12, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Statistical testing of proportion differences with propeller

```{r step5_propeller}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Statistical testing of proportion differences
#-----------------------------------------------

# Prepare data for propeller
cluster_ids <- seurat_obj@meta.data[[celltype.col]]
sample_ids <- seurat_obj@meta.data[[sample.col]]

# Create group vector (condition per sample)
sample_to_condition <- unique(seurat_obj@meta.data[, c(sample.col, condition.col)])
rownames(sample_to_condition) <- sample_to_condition[[sample.col]]
group <- sample_to_condition[sample_ids, condition.col]

# Run propeller test
propeller_results <- propeller(
  clusters = cluster_ids,
  sample = sample_ids,
  group = group
)

# Save results
# FIX: row names hold the cell type labels, so they must be kept (the article
# used row.names = FALSE, which discards them)
write.csv(propeller_results, file.path(diff.dir, "results/propeller_proportion_test.csv"),
          row.names = TRUE)

print(propeller_results)
```

The `PropRatio` column is the ratio of mean proportions between the groups; the
article suggests treating ratios above 1.5 or below 0.67 as biologically
meaningful, alongside the FDR.
